newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Weak crude oil and gold undermine CRB.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Weak crude oil and gold undermine CRB.

text.p: Weakness in energy and precious metals prices, combined with ongoing downtrends in grain prices, pushed the Knight Ridder Commodity Research Bureau Index (CRB) to three month lows Wednesday.

"Weakness in Far East economies this year, with metal and grain purchases by China and Japan down recently, have meant expectations for commodity price inflation have not been fulfilled," Refco's New York economist James Steel said.
The CRB was down 0.01 point midday Wednesday at 241.10, after seeing a morning low at 240.69, the lowest since August.
The Goldman Sachs Commodity Index (GSCI), dominated by the energy sector, was down 0.96 points at 209.21 midday, after coming off five-month highs at 214.78 seen on October 9.

NYFE November CRB futures were up 0.20 points at 240.40, after trending down since early September, while the more liquid CME November GSCI futures were down 0.80 points at 209.40, after slipping from five month highs in early October.

With the exception of the energy sector, most of the 17 U.S. traded commodities in the CRB and the 22 U.S. and European commodities in the GSCI have been weak recently, but the four month old rally in crude oil and refined petroleum products looks to be topping out for now also, analysts said.
NYMEX December crude oil was down 23 cents at $24.11 a barrel midday Wednesday, after seeing the highest levels since the 1991 Gulf War at $25.80 on October 22.

The popular four, nine and 18 day triple-moving average trend-following indicator has turned negative for December crude oil for the first time since late July, with the four-day average below both the nine and 18 day averages.

The standard nine-day relative strength index (RSI) has fallen back below 50 percent for the first time since July also, and the contract is testing the bottom of the standard 14-day Bollinger Band trend-channel indicator, traders said.
Two fundamental factors contributed to the stalling of the rally in crude oil and heating oil, analysts said.

A surge in oil refinery production of distillates (diesel and heating oil) to a record 3.79 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ended October 25, plus the decision by Colonial Pipeline Co to use some of its gasoline line capacity to move distillates from the U.S. Gulf Coast to New York Harbor, has eased fears of heating oil shortages.
"But the Atlantic Basin crude market remains well underpinned by winter product market fundamentals," Smith Barney analyst John Saucer said.

U.S. distillate demand is running 5.2 pct above last year's levels for the first 298 days of 1996, the U.S. Energy Department said Wednesday, while historically low levels of distillate inventories in the U.S. and Europe are seen keeping refineries running near capacity, analysts said.
OPEC is also seen unlikely to raise its production ceiling at its upcoming mid-November meeting.
Meanwhile, precious metals saw a renewed bout of weakness in the past few days, after recovering partially in the past two weeks from a downtrend since early 1996.
COMEX December gold was down 50 cents at $381.10 an ounce midday Wednesday, not far from the life-of-contract lows at $379.00 seen on October 1.
Spot gold bullion was testing key support around $380.00 an ounce, a level breached only once in the past 18 months.
